scope: Semantic review of currently written vendor bundles for checkout, payments, refunds_returns, pricing_tax, and online_invoices. Proposed aliases normalize merchant-observable outcomes while retaining each source claim's vendor, mode, plan, hardware, tender, permission, and recovery qualifiers. This is a review artifact only; it does not edit vendor bundles or assert product compatibility.

alias_groups.rationale: Both let an operator change the quantity of an item before completing payment.
alias_groups.variant_cautions: Shopify describes quantity controls in the cart row. Square permits preselection or editing during item configuration and says relevant quantity fields lock after saving the cart; preserve that workflow limit.

alias_groups.rationale: Both remove an unpaid item from the active cart.
alias_groups.variant_cautions: Shopify documents selected-multiple and clear-all removal as well as one line; Square documents line removal and clear cart with confirmation. Do not assume the same undo behavior.

alias_groups.rationale: Each exposes a customer gratuity choice or merchant-configured tip collection at checkout/POS.
alias_groups.variant_cautions: Shopify claim is eligible POS card checkout; Square documents configurable prompt timing and presets/custom/no-tip; Toast includes default, approval threshold, signature flow; BTCPay describes configurable POS tip feature/percentage presets. Keep supported modes, tender eligibility, calculation basis, settlement timing, and whether UI is merchant- or buyer-facing as claim-level qualifiers. Do not alias Square's 36-hour tip settlement with tip collection.

alias_groups.rationale: All support a cash tender at an in-person checkout and a recorded payment outcome.
alias_groups.variant_cautions: Shopify and Toast calculate change due when amount tendered exceeds balance. Square claim covers cash/check/other recorded tenders and explicitly says Square does not process or transfer the money; it does not currently claim the same change calculation. Keep noncash tender and change behavior separate in detailed acceptance criteria.

alias_groups.rationale: Both describe finishing one sale using more than one tender method until the sale is fully paid.
alias_groups.variant_cautions: Square imposes a five-minute completion window and has a connected Terminal card restriction; Shopify's eligible POS device/method combinations are separate. Toast partial card acceptance below is deliberately excluded because its claims emphasize an open/partially paid check rather than a completed split.

alias_groups.rationale: These claims expose restaurant check allocation into separate guest amounts using seats, items, portions, or equal shares.
alias_groups.variant_cautions: Square item/portion splitting needs Restaurants Plus/Premium with New order and pay; seat splitting requires seat tracking and has limitations on fractional items, modifiers, and recombination. Toast claim includes item/equal/seat options but source-specific workflow and requirements remain intact. Square C016 is a broad summary overlapping C047-C049; keep as a vendor claim if needed but do not count it as another distinct behavior in normalized capability totals.

alias_groups.rationale: Both let staff move an item from one check to another.
alias_groups.variant_cautions: Square also documents course moves and full-check/table merge in the same broader claim; Toast C033 specifically describes moving an item. Avoid treating check merge or payment transfer as the same operation.

alias_groups.rationale: Each supports refunding an eligible order by selected item/quantity or a specified amount, including a full refund.
alias_groups.variant_cautions: Square's claim is specifically linked card refunds and disallows cancellation after submission; Toast also includes charges, tax, tip, full check and multi-tender refund distribution; Shopify describes POS order returns and eligible order conditions. Preserve tender-specific limits and refund destination.

alias_groups.rationale: Both document refunding tip value as part of refund handling; Shopify makes a separate-tip refund explicit and Toast includes tips in its broad refund scope.
alias_groups.variant_cautions: Toast's claim does not assert that tip can always be refunded separately from merchandise, only that tip is a supported refund component. Keep Shopify's independent tip refund capability distinct from Toast's inclusive scope until Toast evidence establishes separate handling.

alias_groups.rationale: These support presenting, configuring, or delivering proof of payment through print, email, SMS, app, or an automatic/default route.
alias_groups.variant_cautions: These claims document receipt-channel choice after checkout. Shopify includes Shop app and no receipt; Square offers printed/text/email according to receipt screen; Toast digital mode offers text/email or print for in-store order. Device, consent and payment-state conditions stay attached.

alias_groups.rationale: Square exposes reprint of paper receipt or resend of digital receipt from transaction history.
alias_groups.variant_cautions: This is a Square-only capability in current corpus, distinct from choosing receipt destination at checkout; gift and declined-payment receipts have separate paths.

alias_groups.rationale: Both configure receipt behavior to suppress or override per-transaction customer channel choice.
alias_groups.variant_cautions: Square skip mode sends automatically to opted-in customers and is device-local; Toast supports device receipt mode overrides and transaction toggles. Do not assume identical consent/default behavior.

collisions.reason: This is an intentional exact canonical-key collision across Shopify and Square for the same pre-payment line removal outcome. Keep one normalized capability with vendor-specific confirmation, multiple/all-item, and recovery variants.

notes: Inspected all current vendor bundles; category and field labels differ between files. `card-components.json` claims describe developer SDK integration behavior, not merchant-facing POS operator-guide capabilities. Keep them in a distinct integration layer except where the normalized concept explicitly names SDK lifecycle. `shopify-operations.json` has one in-scope payment claim (gift-card issue), but it is gift-card issuance, not a customer checkout payment/refund; no alias proposed.

Do not merge generic discounts. Square SQC-C009-C012 cover configured preset/automatic discounts and exclusions; Shopify SHC-C003-C006 cover custom cart/line discounts, best eligible combination and third-party discount apps; Toast TOS-C011 covers rule/authorization-based discount availability. They share a pricing domain but not the same operator-observable trigger or application behavior.

Do not merge tax claims yet. Shopify SHC-C007 documents toggling applicable tax rates for cart/all or selected product; Square SQC-C027-C029 documents creating rates, inclusive/additive calculation, and exemptions/rules. Distinct policy configuration and application semantics are represented.

Do not equate tender split with partial payment or invoice underpayment. Shopify SHC-C011 completes one order with multiple methods while SHC-C012 leaves an order partially paid; Toast TOS-C007-C008 leaves an open balance after partial card authorization; BTCPay BTM-C011 allows partial payment on a request, and BTM-C029 tracks a partially paid invoice. These should retain different lifecycle and reconciliation keys.

BTCPay invoice creation and payment requests are not aliases: BTM-C003 creates an invoice/order context, while BTM-C010 creates a shareable longer-lived request with optional customer prompts. BTM-C004-C005 and C027-C031 describe payment status/exceptions, not customer tender selection. Avoid folding invoice settlement lifecycle into POS checkout payment completion.

Toast TOS-C030 captures the clear lifecycle boundary: void check before capture, refund after capture. Square SQC-C044 is open-ticket/check void before preparation, while SQC-C043 is issuer release of a pending card authorization after cancellation/decline. These are related void vocabulary but not aliases: the Square cases are not proof of a general post-capture void action. Square U011 correctly leaves general completed-payment cashier void unresolved. Empty cover-count table hold in SQC-C052 differs from Toast TOS-C027 (unfired order held from kitchen/payment), so preserve these as separate operational states.

Square checkout bundle has meaningful overlap: SQC-C016 is a broad check-splitting summary for the more precise C047-C049; C045 and C055 both describe reopen-check payment-method keep/remove behavior; C033 and C053 overlap receipt channel/reprint behavior. Preserve all claim IDs, but treat these as evidence summaries rather than separate normalized capabilities. SQC-C031 bundles presets, calculation basis, custom tip and round-up thresholds; split into individually measurable behaviors if this bundle is later used to generate tests. SQC-C014 bundles cash, check, gift-card and generic other tender into one record-only statement; keep cash receipt separate from other-tender logging when implementing acceptance tests. SQC-C026 bundles ordinary Bitcoin tender recording and Loyalty points outcome; reporting integration and customer rewards should be evaluated independently.

Square refund claims are better decomposed than the first pass: C035 item/amount scope, C038 one-year window, C040 fee/funding source, C041 external-tender record-only refund, C042 incompletely documented tax recalculation, C056 required associated tax language. C039 cancellation limitation is a distinct workflow guard. Do not interpret itemized refund selection as verified automatic tax calculation.

Bitcoin assertions should remain qualified by source: Square SQC-C023 now cites the Bitcoin Wallet help page and Terms for custody, settlement and withdrawal, and should not imply self-custody within Square. Terms say Square acts as agent for Bitcoin Payments and payment to Block satisfies buyer obligation; wallet help says Square is custodian while funds remain in Square wallet. Terms permit deposits subject to controls while wallet help says external deposits are currently unavailable: retain this documentation conflict rather than resolving by inference. Square Bitcoin eligibility, New York/territory exclusions, account verification, USD conversion, caps, network delays and gift-card-only POS refunds remain claim qualifiers/tradeoffs.

Bitcoin hypotheses are proposals, not evidence that an incumbent supports self-custody, Lightning node control, mixed Bitcoin/card splits, no eligibility gate, or tax/refund parity. In BTCPay claims, noncustodial wallet signing/broadcast is evidenced separately from receipt/settlement states; do not infer a payment is final solely because a checkout UI reports an invoice state. For this operator-facing normalization, card SDK claims are not aliases of POS terminal workflows even where the same card-present action occurs; they describe integration responsibilities, not a merchant’s out-of-box checkout behavior.

Square SQC-C013 describes account operator tender configuration/order across devices, while Shopify SHC-C009 describes cashier tender choice at checkout; do not normalize these as one behavior. Similarly, Toast TOS-C007-C008 describe partial authorization/open balance, not completed split tender.

Exact canonical key collision scan found only `checkout.cart.item.remove` within the requested checkout/payment/pricing/refund scope. A separate `cash_drawer.report.view` duplicate exists in Square operations but is outside this review. Semantic overlap without exact key equality is listed as alias/overlap notes above.
